newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel clears sale of Israel Edible to CPC.
newsitem.headline: Israel clears sale of Israel Edible to CPC.

text.p: Israel's anti-trust authority has approved the sale of Koor Industries's 24.5 percent holding in Israel Edible Products to CPC International Inc., Koor said on Wednesday.

Koor said Englewood Cliffs, N.J.-based CPC, whose products also include Skippy peanut butter and Mazola oil, paid 122.22 million shekels ($37.5 million) for the holding in Israel Edible, which is also known as Tami. Koor is Israel's largest holding company.
The acquisition brings CPC's total stake in Israel Edible to about 84 percent.

CPC acquired a 51 percent holding in Israel Edible in 1993 for $43 million and then helped introduce CPC products, such as Hellman's mayonnaise, to the line. CPC brands now make up 12 percent to 15 percent of Israel Edible's product line, the company said.

Israel Edible produced 90 percent of Israel's margarine as well as soups, sauces, breakfast cereals, snacks and chocolates. The company said sales last year were $250 million, making it Israel's third-largest dry goods producer.
Koor has said the sale is part of its strategy to pull out of activities outside of its core businesses in telecommunications, electronics, agrochemicals, building materials and energy distribution.
Sources said this week that Koor was in talks to sell its Shemen Industries subsidiary, which makes edible oils and personal care products.
